parsed.why: Criminalises same-sex conduct and detains trans-appearing people up to six months under a gender-expression charge. Documented beatings, a visitor held 44 days after a fake dating-app sting, and forced detransition in custody. Hotels refuse same-sex couples. Severe state-directed exposure.

Constitutional protection and 2018 decriminalisation, but a 2026 amendment restricts recognition and the criminal code dropped trans-specific offences. Traveller-facing friction: airport stop despite valid ID, railway police groping, degrading railway custody. Policy note calls police abuse limited.

Extremism designation with 101 convictions, venue raids, and propaganda laws reaching expression. No legal gender change, and marriage is void for trans people. A detainee died in custody and a conversion-therapy centre held a trans woman. Official hostility, with no hate-crime recourse.

Statutory trans-specific protections, administrative gender recognition, prison placement by choice, and an equal age of consent. Downgraded by a survey finding two-thirds of trans people report physical violence, a trans murder with prosecution, and hospital mistreatment with a pending complaint. Strong rule of law.

Constitutional gender-identity protection, no surgery requirement, full hate-crime and conversion-therapy protections, and a ban on intersex surgery. Low victimisation at the regional low end. The main exposure is a prison-section lag documented by a 2018 award and a 2024 dissertation, now largely remedied by female-section placement.
